A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DECO and DECO-50. All 21 pages of v3 and 25 pages of v4, including their appendices, support comparison. The existing material is retained; v4 principally adds Appendix C.

before.justification: v3 reports original real-robot evaluations, tactile-adapter ablations, distribution-shift tests, and encoder comparisons in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds DECO simulation results on four benchmarks in Appendix C. These qualify independently of the externally sourced comparator scores.

M1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a T5 language encoder to DECO for language-conditioned RoboTwin evaluation, a limited architectural and input adaptation. The original multimodal pathways, flow-matching objective, two-stage training, and tactile adapter remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v4 extends evaluation beyond DECO-50 to LIBERO general manipulation, 50 language-conditioned RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, eight UniVTAC vision-tactile tasks, and 11 DexJoCo dexterous tasks. Added scenarios include unseen instructions and randomized objects, cameras, lighting, and textures. The original real-world coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The original ACT, DP/DP.t, and DECO-variant comparisons remain. Tables 21–26 add comparisons involving OpenVLA/OpenVLA-OFT, π0/π0.5, X-VLA, StarVLA-OFT, ABot-M0, LingBot-VLA, UniVTAC, FTP-1, N0-VTLA, DP-T, and GR00T N1.5. Many comparator scores are explicitly sourced from previous reports rather than newly run baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces substantial new evaluation designs: 50 episodes per task for LIBERO and DexJoCo, 100 for RoboTwin and UniVTAC, and a single jointly trained UniVTAC checkpoint executing 16-action chunks at stride 2. It also documents randomization protocols and action-budget/stride controls. Existing real-robot settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds UniVTAC comparisons with and without tactile input, taskwise timeout/slippage diagnostics, and action-stride/budget sensitivity tests. RoboTwin and DexJoCo additionally evaluate environmental randomization. These substantially extend the retained fusion, pathway-assignment, encoder-capacity, and OOD analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix C.3 newly specifies identical evaluation seeds for the UniVTAC comparison. Existing Wilson 95% confidence intervals remain unchanged. The simulation additions provide no training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are unchanged. New results include DECO averages of 94.2% on LIBERO, 85.3% on RoboTwin, and 56.4%/58.0% on DexJoCo rand-obj/rand-full; both DECO and DECO.p average 82.1% on UniVTAC. Tables 21–26 and accompanying diagnostics add substantial new findings, not same-setting improvements over v3.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, flow-matching loss and inference update, conditioning equations, and tactile-embedding formulation in Section 3 are unchanged. Appendix C adds no formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about decoupled conditioning, efficient tactile adaptation, DECO-50, and real-robot performance. The simulation appendix supplies additional evidence without redefining these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 adds localized interpretations of action-budget effects and the absent average tactile benefit, attributing HDMI timeouts to visual alignment and other failures to slippage. It also explicitly qualifies UniVTAC comparisons because pretraining and per-task versus multitask protocols differ. Existing interpretations and limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 newly states that simulation code and trained weights for all four benchmarks are available at the existing repository. It also supplies benchmark-specific encoder and action-execution details. The original hardware, preprocessing, implementation, and hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: New references support the simulation benchmarks and comparators, including LIBERO, UniVTAC, DexJoCo, OpenVLA-OFT, and newer VLA/tactile policies. Appendix C adds limited positioning concerning model size and pretraining requirements; Section 2 and the original novelty framing remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 appends Appendix C with four benchmark subsections and short diagnostic discussions. Reference venue abbreviations, citation suffixes, and the version stamp also change. The main narrative and Appendices A–B undergo no substantive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: Tables 21–26 substantially expand the tabular presentation with benchmark comparisons, an eight-task failure breakdown, and separate DexJoCo randomization displays, including explanatory footnotes. Existing Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–20 retain their content and layout; references reflow and appendix pagination shifts.

improvement.justification: v3's empirical evidence was confined to the authors' real-robot dataset. Appendix C substantially strengthens assessment beyond that setting through external benchmarks and environmental variation. The UniVTAC null tactile result and stride/failure diagnostics also clarify applicability limits. Heterogeneous comparator training and missing simulation uncertainty estimates limit ranking claims, but the disclosed qualifications and more diagnostic evidence provide a substantial net quality improvement.
